mainTopic: Why courts stopped making an אלמנה swear for her כתובה, and how far that rule reaches
overview: This amud discusses the משנה's rule that courts stopped making an אלמנה take a שבועה before collecting her כתובה from the יתומים. The גמרא first suggests the reason is the story of a widow who swore, truthfully as far as she knew, about a deposited gold dinar, and lost a child. Then it asks why a גרושה still swears, and answers that an אלמנה, who works hard for the orphans, may talk herself into swearing falsely. Next come two versions of what רב and שמואל held: does the rule apply only in בית דין, or even outside it? In the נהרדעא version, רב never lets a widow swear, which is why he never collects a כתובה for her. Stories follow about widows before רב הונא and רבה בר רב הונא, including the rule that a widow who swears on her own (קופצת) may collect. רב יהודה then gives a way to let widows collect: a נדר in court and a שבועה outside it. Finally, the גמרא returns to שמואל's statement that a גרושה is made to swear. It challenges it with a letter from ארץ ישראל about a divorcée who collected with only a נדר, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה needed to say this, so we would not think חכמים were lenient
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: without the משנה we might have thought חכמים eased things for the אלמנה, so the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: [You might have said that] because of her appeal for remarriage, חכמים were lenient with her. So the משנה teaches us [that this is not so].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer it started before this section. It explains why the משנה had to spell out its rule about the אלמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that חכמים, who often make things easier for women so they can remarry, would also go easy here. The משנה's wording shows that this leniency does not apply, so the line is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Appeal, attractiveness (here: making her a more attractive match for remarriage)
It teaches us (the source is telling us something new)

phrases.english: Because of desirability
phrases.notes: חינא means her appeal as a match for remarrying. This finishes a 'you might have thought' line from just before.

phrases.english: the Sages were lenient with her,
it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a necessary teaching ('you might have thought otherwise')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because חכמים are lenient with women for the sake of remarriage, an אלמנה might collect more easily.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that this leniency does not apply here.

steps.title: Why did the courts stop making widows swear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'they refrained from making her swear' and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They refrained from making her swear': What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks why the courts stopped giving the אלמנה a שבועה. This question sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said an אלמנה collects from יתומים only with a שבועה, but then courts stopped making her swear. The גמרא wants to know what made them change.

keyTerms.meaning: From making her take an oath

phrases.english: They refrained from making her swear:
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the courts stopped making an אלמנה swear.

steps.title: A suggested reason: the story of the widow and the gold dinar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is a story told by רב כהנא (or רב יהודה in the name of רב): a widow was given a gold dinar to look after, and it ended up baked into bread given to a poor man.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of רב כהנא's statement, as רב כהנא said (and some say רב יהודה said in the name of רב): There was a case of a man in years of famine who deposited a gold dinar with a widow. She put it in a jug of flour, baked it into bread without knowing, and gave the bread to a poor man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer by bringing a story about an oath. Here it tells the first part of the story: how the coin went missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אילימא ('if you say') marks this as a suggestion the גמרא will test. The idea is that oaths are so dangerous that courts stopped imposing them on widows. The widow did not know the coin was in the flour, so she lost it by accident.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggested answer that will be tested)

steps.confusionAlert: אילימא is only a suggestion. Do not assume this is the גמרא's final reason until you see how it is tested.

phrases.english: If you say it is because of the statement of Rav Kahana –
as Rav Kahana said;

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
There was an incident with a man during years of famine,
who deposited a gold dinar with a widow;
and she placed it in a jug of flour,
and baked it into bread,
and gave it to a poor man;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a suggested answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested: the courts stopped because of the danger of oaths, shown by רב כהנא's story.

steps.title: The widow swears she did not benefit, and her child dies
steps.stepSummary: The owner asks for his dinar. The widow swears by her children's lives that she got no benefit from it, and soon one of her children dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: After some time the owner of the dinar came and said to her: Give me my dinar. She said: May deadly poison take effect on one of that woman's children if I benefited at all from your dinar! They said: only a few days passed before one of her children died.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The widow takes a strong oath that she did not benefit, and is punished with the death of a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As far as she knew, her oath was true. She had lost the coin by accident and given the bread to charity. Still she was punished, which shows how serious an oath is.

phrases.english: After some time the owner of the dinar came,
and said to her: Give me my dinar.
She said to him:
May deadly poison take effect
phrases.notes: Literally 'may poison benefit,' a play on the word for benefit that ends her oath.

phrases.english: on one of the children of that woman,
phrases.notes: 'That woman' means herself. She avoids saying 'my children' directly.

phrases.english: if I benefited at all from your dinar!
They said: not even a few days passed
before one of her children died;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an oath she believed was true brought a heavy punishment on the widow.

steps.title: The lesson of חכמים: a false oath is far worse
steps.stepSummary: חכמים hear the story and draw a קל וחומר: if someone who swore truthfully is punished like this, someone who swears falsely is punished all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: When חכמים heard about it, they said: If someone who swears truthfully is punished like this, someone who swears falsely, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים give the lesson of the story. They argue from a lighter case (a true oath) to a heavier one (a false oath).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר. The point is that oaths are dangerous, which is why the גמרא suggested that courts stopped making widows swear.

keyTerms.meaning: How much more so (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: The story teaches that even a seemingly true oath can bring punishment. This is the suggested reason the courts stopped making widows swear.

phrases.english: and when the Sages heard about the matter, they said:
If one who swears truthfully – is punished like this,
one who swears falsely –
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the lesson of the story told in steps 3-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a truthful oath is punished this way, a false oath is punished all the more.

steps.title: Why was she punished if she told the truth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the widow was punished, and answers that the coin took up space in the dough, so she did benefit a little.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was she punished? Because she benefited from the space the dinar took up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up a puzzle in the story. If she really got no benefit, why was she punished? It answers that she did get a small benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coin filled a little space in the loaf, so she needed slightly less flour. That tiny benefit made her oath 'I benefited not at all' untrue, which explains the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The space taken up by the dinar

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how careful a person must be with an oath. Even a tiny unknown benefit makes 'not at all' false.

phrases.english: What is the reason she was punished?
Because she benefited from the space of the dinar.
phrases.notes: The coin took up room in the loaf, so she used a little less flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clears up a detail of the story in steps 4-5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a widow who swore truthfully was punished.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She did benefit slightly, since the coin took up space in the dough and saved her flour.

steps.title: How can her oath be called true?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים could call the widow 'one who swore truthfully' if she really did benefit from the coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'one who swore truthfully' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a problem with the קל וחומר from step 5. If the widow benefited a little, then her oath was not fully true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the coin took up space in the dough, so she did get a small benefit. That makes her oath technically false. So why did the חכמים describe her as someone who swore truthfully?

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'one who swears truthfully'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a wording problem created by step 6's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the oath can be called truthful when she did benefit

steps.title: She was like someone who swore truthfully
steps.stepSummary: The answer: she was 'like' one who swore truthfully, because as far as she knew her oath was true.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: like one who swore truthfully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים did not mean her oath was truly true. They meant it was close to true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She honestly believed she had gotten nothing from the coin, so her oath only looked true. This makes the lesson stronger: even an honest mistake in an oath brought a harsh punishment. The גמרא's suggestion is that this danger is why חכמים stopped making widows swear. The next step tests that idea.
steps.whatToRemember: Even an oath that is false only by a tiny, innocent mistake is treated with great seriousness. The גמרא offered this danger as a possible reason why חכמים stopped making an אלמנה swear, but step 9 challenges it and step 10 adds what makes a widow different.

phrases.english: Like one who swears truthfully.
phrases.notes: The little letter כ ("like") is the whole answer. It was not truly true, only close to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase means 'like' a true oath. She thought it was true, but it was slightly false.

steps.title: Then why not a divorced woman too?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is fear of a false oath, a גרושה should also be exempt from swearing. Yet שמואל says she does swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of this, why only a widow? A divorced woman too! Why then did רבי זירא say in the name of שמואל: they taught this only about a widow, but a divorced woman we do make swear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story as the reason for the rule. The fear of a false oath should apply to every woman, not only widows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger of swearing falsely applies to anyone. But שמואל rules that a גרושה still swears to collect her כתובה. So the story alone cannot explain why only an אלמנה is exempt.

phrases.english: If it is because of this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the story of the dinar and the fear of a false oath.

phrases.english: why specifically a widow?
Even a divorced woman as well!

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Why then did Rabbi Zeira say that Shmuel said:
They taught this only about a widow,
but a divorced woman, we make her swear?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם הָא, מַאי אִירְיָא אַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story (steps 3-8) as the reason for the rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dinar story is the reason widows are not made to swear
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason applies to everyone, but שמואל limits the rule to widows, so the reason seems too broad.

steps.title: A widow is different
steps.stepSummary: An אלמנה works hard for the יתומים, so she may convince herself she has a right to swear falsely.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow is different. Because of the benefit the orphans get from all her efforts for them, she may come to rule for herself that it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the worry is stronger for a widow than for a divorced woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow stays in the house and does a lot of work for the orphans. She may feel they owe her something. So she might tell herself it is fine to swear she was never paid part of her כתובה, even if she was. A divorced woman has no such reason to fool herself.

keyTerms.meaning: to rule for herself that something is permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exemption is based on a special risk that only an אלמנה has. That is why a גרושה still swears.

phrases.english: A widow is different;

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְהָהִיא הֲנָאָה דְּקָא טָרְחָה קַמֵּי דְּיַתְמֵי,
phrases.english: because of that benefit, since she works hard for the orphans,
she will come to permit it to herself.
phrases.notes: She talks herself into thinking she may swear, even though she already took part of her money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a widow has a special reason to fool herself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fear of a false oath should apply equally to every woman
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a widow, who works for the orphans, is likely to justify a false oath to herself, so only she is exempt

steps.title: Only in court is she not made to swear
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that רב and שמואל both say the rule applies only to an oath in בית דין. Outside בית דין, she is made to swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: רב and שמואל both say they taught this only in court, but outside court we make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limits the משנה's rule. The widow is spared only from an oath taken in בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said חכמים stopped making the widow swear. Here רב and שמואל say this applies only to an oath in בית דין. Outside בית דין, she can still be made to swear and then collect.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
It is Rav and Shmuel who both say:
They taught this only in court,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין – מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: but outside of court, we make her swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on how far the משנה's rule reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow is not made to swear in בית דין, but she is made to swear outside בית דין.

steps.title: But רב never collects for a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the report about רב. His own practice seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב allowed a widow to swear outside בית דין, she could then collect her כתובה. Yet רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow. This suggests he would not let her swear even outside בית דין.

phrases.english: Is that so? But Rav does not collect
a marriage contract payment for a widow!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַב לָא מַגְבֵּי כְּתוּבָּה לְאַרְמַלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רב allows a widow to swear outside בית דין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's practice of never collecting for a widow shows he would not have her swear anywhere.

steps.title: The difficulty remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the question has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge against this version has no answer. The next step brings a different version of the statement that avoids the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for the clash between this report about רב and רב's own practice. Instead, step 14 brings a different version of the statement that fits רב's practice.
steps.whatToRemember: Saying קַשְׁיָא means the challenge has no answer. Here it undermines the report that רב allows a widow to swear outside בית דין, and step 14 brings another version instead.
steps.confusionAlert: קַשְׁיָא here is not a new question. It is the גמרא's way of saying it has no answer to the question it just asked.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes step 12's challenge without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against the report about רב remains unanswered.

steps.title: The נהרדעא version of רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: In נהרדעא the statement was taught differently. שמואל says the oath is skipped only in בית דין, and outside בית דין she swears. רב says she does not swear even outside בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught it the way we just said. In נהרדעא they taught it like this: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, the rule applies only in בית דין, but outside בית דין they make her swear. רב said: even outside בית דין they do not make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: After the question on the first version had no answer, the גמרא brings a different version of the statement. In this version רב and שמואל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סורא version from Step 11, רב agreed that she swears outside בית דין. That clashed with רב's practice of never collecting a כתובה for a widow. In the נהרדעא version רב says she never swears at all, so the problem from Step 12 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Another major Babylonian Torah city, שמואל's home
They make her take an oath

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the סורא version רב agrees with שמואל. In the נהרדעא version רב is stricter and says she never swears.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught it this way.
phrases.notes: "This way" means the version from Step 11, where רב and שמואל agree.

phrases.english: In Neharde'a they taught it this way:
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
They taught this only about an oath in court,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין – מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: but outside court, they make her swear.
And Rav said:
Even outside court as well
they do not make her swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different version of Step 11 that avoids the unanswered question of Steps 12-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: she swears outside בית דין. רב: she does not swear even outside בית דין.

steps.title: רב is consistent with his own practice
steps.stepSummary: This version fits רב's known practice, because רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב follows his own reasoning, since רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the נהרדעא version matches what we already know about רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב holds that a widow can never be made to swear, she has no way to collect from the orphans. That is why רב never collects a כתובה for her. The fact that was a question in Step 12 now becomes support.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with himself

phrases.english: Rav follows his own reasoning,
since Rav does not collect a כתובה for a widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that Step 14's version of רב fits the practice that was a problem in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate version of the statement removes the contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב agrees she swears outside בית דין, which clashes with his practice.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds she never swears, so he never collects for her.

steps.title: Why not have her take a vow instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב does not have the widow take a vow in place of an oath and then collect for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him make her take a vow, and then collect the כתובה for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's practice. There is a simpler option than leaving her with nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if an oath is not allowed, the משנה offers a vow as a replacement. A vow would protect the orphans in a similar way. So why does רב refuse to collect at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him make her take a vow
A vow, which makes something forbidden

phrases.english: But let him make her take a vow and collect it for her!
phrases.notes: The משנה said a widow can take a vow in place of the oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's refusal to collect a כתובה for a widow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow can replace the oath, so there is no need to deny her the כתובה.

steps.title: In רב's time vows were taken lightly
steps.stepSummary: In רב's days people did not take vows seriously, so a vow would not protect the orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the years of רב, vows were treated lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: a vow was not reliable in רב's generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow only works if people fear breaking it. In רב's time people did not, so a widow might vow falsely. That would hurt the orphans, so רב did not rely on vows.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows were light, taken without seriousness

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's practice came from the conditions of his time, not from a rule that a widow can never collect.

phrases.english: In Rav's years, vows were treated lightly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vow could replace the oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vows were not taken seriously then, so they could not be trusted.

steps.title: A widow swears on her own before רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A widow came to רב הונא, who said he could not help because of רב's practice. She answered that the only worry is that she already took something, and she swore that she had not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain widow came before רב הונא. He said: What can I do for you? רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow. She said: Is the reason anything other than the worry that I already took something from my כתובה? As ה׳ of Hosts lives, I did not benefit from my כתובה at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests רב's practice. It sets up רב הונא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow points out that רב's concern is only that she may have already been paid something. She removes that concern by swearing on her own, without בית דין asking her to.

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do for you?
As ה׳ of Hosts lives (an oath)

phrases.english: A certain woman came before Rav Huna;
he said to her: What can I do for you,
since Rav does not collect a כתובה for a widow.
She said to him: Is the reason anything
other than that perhaps I took something from my כתובה?
As ה׳ of Hosts lives,
I did not benefit from my כתובה at all!
phrases.notes: In the language of an oath, "אם" means "I did not."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests רב's practice from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: a widow takes an oath on her own to collect her כתובה.

steps.title: רב agrees when she swears on her own
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that רב agrees that a widow who jumps ahead and swears on her own may collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רב agrees in the case of a woman who jumps ahead and swears.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his ruling on the widow's case: her oath is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only refused to have בית דין impose an oath on her. If she steps forward and swears on her own, as this widow did, her oath is accepted and she collects. This limits how far רב's practice goes.

keyTerms.meaning: One who jumps ahead, a woman who swears on her own

steps.whatToRemember: Even according to רב, a widow who swears on her own (קופצת) collects her כתובה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Rav agrees in the case of one who jumps ahead.
phrases.notes: Literally "one who jumps." She jumps in and swears before anyone asks her to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A widow who swears on her own initiative collects her כתובה even according to רב.

steps.title: A widow comes before רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A widow came before רבה בר רב הונא. He told her he could not help, since both רב and his father רב הונא do not collect a כתובה for a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain widow came before רבה בר רב הונא. He said: What can I do for you? רב does not collect a כתובה for a widow, and my father, my master, does not collect a כתובה for a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story about a widow. This sets up the next part of the story, which continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא adds his father רב הונא as another authority who does not collect for a widow. This sets up a second chance for a widow to find a way around the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: My father, my master (a respectful way to say his father)

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: A certain woman came before Rabba bar Rav Huna;
he said to her: What can I do for you,
since Rav does not collect a כתובה for a widow,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַבָּא מָרִי לָא מַגְבֵּי כְּתוּבָּה לְאַרְמַלְתָּא.
phrases.english: and my father, my master, does not collect a כתובה for a widow.
phrases.notes: "My father" here is רב הונא, from the previous story.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second story on the same theme as Steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבה בר רב הונא declines, citing both רב and רב הונא.

steps.title: The widow asks for food money and is refused
steps.stepSummary: The widow asks רבה בר רב הונא for מזונות. He refuses, quoting רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: a woman who demands her כתובה in court has no right to מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Then give me food money. He said to her: You don't have food money either, because רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a woman who demands her כתובה in court has no right to food money.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step goes on. The widow could not get her כתובה, so she asks for her food support instead, and רבה בר רב הונא turns her down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow is normally fed from her late husband's property. But שמואל rules that once she demands her כתובה in court, she loses that support. So the widow is left with nothing: no כתובה because of רב, and no מזונות because of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Food support a widow gets from her late husband's property
A woman who demands payment of her כתובה

phrases.english: She said to him: Give me sustenance.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: מְזוֹנֵי נָמֵי לֵית לִיךְ;
phrases.english: He said to her: You do not have sustenance either;
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who demands her marriage contract in court
has no sustenance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the widow's story from step 20. After being refused her כתובה, she asks for מזונות and is refused again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: a woman who demands her כתובה in court loses her right to מזונות.

steps.title: The widow's curse and its effect
steps.stepSummary: The widow curses רבה בר רב הונא for ruling against her using the strict sides of two different authorities. He turns his chair over and sets it upright to fulfill the curse, but still becomes weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: May his chair be overturned! You treated me according to two different people! They overturned his chair and set it upright again, and even so he was not saved from weakness.
steps.whatsHappening: The widow gets angry and curses the judge. The גמרא tells us the curse had a real effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her complaint is that he took the strict side from two sources: רב (no כתובה) and שמואל (no מזונות). Together they left her with nothing. He tried to fulfill the curse in a small way by tipping his chair over, but he still became weak. This shows the ruling was seen as unfair to her.

keyTerms.meaning: His chair, the seat of his authority as a judge
Like two (people); following two different opinions

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that combining the strict sides of two opinions against a weak person, like a widow, can be unfair. This leads into רב יהודה's effort to let widows collect.

phrases.english: She said to him: Overturn his chair,
phrases.notes: This is a curse: may he lose his position as a judge.

phrases.english: you treated me according to two people!
phrases.notes: The two are רב, who gives her no כתובה, and שמואל, who gives her no food support.

phrases.english: They overturned his chair and set it upright,
and even so he was not saved from weakness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The widow reacts to the double refusal in steps 20 and 21, and the story ends with what happened to the judge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow's curse on a judge who combined two strict opinions against her took effect.

steps.title: רב יהודה's method to let widows collect
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells רב ירמיה ביראה to have a widow take a נדר in court and a שבועה outside of court, and to let him hear about it, because he wants to put this into practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to רב ירמיה ביראה: Make her take a vow in court, and make her swear outside of court, and let the news reach my ears, because I want to act on this.
steps.whatsHappening: A new short story. רב יהודה, a student of שמואל, gives practical instructions so that widows can collect their כתובה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court won't give a widow a שבועה, as the משנה says. So רב יהודה splits it up. Inside the court she takes only a נדר, and the real שבועה happens outside the court. He wants to hear that it was done, so that collecting by a widow becomes accepted practice, unlike רב's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: A practical action, putting a ruling into practice

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב יהודה is ignoring the משנה. The משנה only stops the court from giving her a שבועה. Here the court gives only a נדר, and the שבועה happens outside of court.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִרְמְיָה בִּירָאָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to Rav Yirmeya Bira'a:
Make her vow in court,
and make her swear outside of court,
and let the report come and fall into my ears,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָעֵינָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאֶעֱבֵיד בָּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: for I want to be able to put it into practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִרְמְיָה בִּירָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stories showing רב's students refusing widows, רב יהודה shows the other approach and actively lets widows collect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow may collect her כתובה by taking a נדר in court and a שבועה outside of court.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. רב and his students would not collect a כתובה for a widow. רב יהודה found a way for her to collect: a נדר inside court and a שבועה outside.

steps.title: שמואל limits the משנה to a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a statement mentioned earlier. רבי זירא says in the name of שמואל that the משנה's rule (no oath) applies only to an אלמנה, but a גרושה is made to swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רבי זירא said in the name of שמואל: They taught this only about a widow, but a divorced woman is made to swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is starting a new section. It goes back to look closely at a statement of רבי זירא in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the court does not make a widow swear in order to collect. שמואל says this applies only to an אלמנה. A גרושה is made to swear and then collects. The next step challenges this: does it mean a נדר is not enough for a גרושה?

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself" — returning to look closely at a statement mentioned earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This signals the גמרא is going back to examine a statement it mentioned before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only about a widow,
but a divorcée, they do make her swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the widow stories behind and opens a new section analyzing שמואל's statement on the scope of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule of no oath applies only to an אלמנה. A גרושה is made to swear and then collects.

steps.title: A letter from ארץ ישראל shows a divorcée collecting with only a vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it is true that a נדר does not work for a גרושה. It brings a letter from ארץ ישראל about a divorced woman who took a נדר, forbidding all the world's produce on herself, that she had received only a few worn-out items from her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean a divorcée who was made to take a vow cannot collect? But they sent a letter from ארץ ישראל: 'So-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, received a גט from אחא בר הידיא, who is called איה מרי. She vowed and forbade all the produce of the world on herself, declaring that all she received from her כתובה was one coat, one book of תהלים, a book of איוב, and a book of משלי, all worn out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's rule from the last step. It brings a real case from ארץ ישראל where a divorced woman collected with only a נדר, not a שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said a גרושה is made to swear, which suggests a נדר is not enough for her. But this letter shows a divorced woman whose נדר was accepted in place of a שבועה. If a נדר worked for her, why does רבי זירא say a גרושה must swear?

keyTerms.meaning: They made her take a נדר (a vow), instead of a שבועה
They sent from there, from ארץ ישראל
She vowed and made something forbidden to herself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up נדר and שבועה here. In a נדר she makes food forbidden to herself if she is lying. In a שבועה she swears using ה׳'s name. The whole question is whether the lighter נדר is enough for a divorcée.

phrases.english: And a divorcée whom they made take a vow, she cannot collect?!
phrases.notes: This is aimed at רבי זירא's rule from the last step, that a גרושה must swear.

phrases.english: But didn't they send from there:
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל. What follows is a court letter they sent.

phrases.english: "How so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so,
received a bill of divorce from the hand
of Acha bar Hidya
who is called 'Ayya Mari';
and she vowed and forbade
the produce of the world upon herself
phrases.notes: She made all food forbidden to herself if her statement was false. This is the נדר in place of a שבועה.

phrases.english: that she did not receive from her marriage contract
anything except one coat,
and one book of Psalms,
and a book of Job,
and Proverbs, all worn out;

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְרוּשָׁה דְּאַדְּרַהּ לָא?! וְהָא שְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבי זירא's rule in step 24 implies, that a גרושה must take a שבועה and a נדר is not enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא in the name of שמואל: a גרושה is made to swear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A letter from ארץ ישראל records a divorced woman who collected her כתובה after taking only a נדר. That shows a נדר is enough for a גרושה, which seems to contradict the rule that she must swear.
